widgets_values:
# READ ME FIRST


**NOTE ABOUT SOUND LEVELS (LUFS)**:

- "Normalising" will raise (or reduce) the inbound audio level based on the loudest moment in all of it. This makes it the best level control at this stage without effecting the sound (compression, eq, expanding, reverb, and all that stuff, leave all that to post production imo).

- I set ambient levels to about -40 LUFs, dialogue audio to -23 or -16 LUFS, depending on level I want. For a guide, Spotify forces all audio to -14 LUFS, but you want to leave some headroom for post-production and to be sure to avoid clipping, so I dont go above -16 LUFS and lean into -23 more often.  

**ISSUES WITH LIPSYNC WHEN DRIVEN BY AUDIO OF DIALOGUE THAT HAS A LOT OF SILENT MOMENTS**:

- LTX 2.3 I find using audio in often doesnt work for lipsync and the mouth wont move if there isnt a lot of audio dialogue. The trick is to add ambient audio in to the full length just room or environment sound (see the audio merge node, adjust LUFS to get levels, use "mean" to blend the two audio files - dialogue and ambient, but watch out for clipping, also you dont want the ambient audio driving action, just enough volume to not be dead silence). 

- This wasnt needed in LTX 2. but is needed in LTX 2.3. I downloaded 10 seconds of room ambience from freesound.org. You dont have to add it to the resulting video and it doesnt have to be audible, just something that is getting rid of the absolute silence should work. If you have a lot of dialogue then it usually isnt needed. - Mark, May 2026.

- put longest audio in "audio1" slot of audio merge
- confirm the correct audio selection is connected to the next stage node.
- confirm you have connected this audio to the LTXVConcatAVLatent node.
- Connect the audio output option you want saved to the video combine node in the final output.

If you get weird NaN errors with FFMPEG confirm the preview is the correct length, and confirm both audio files inbound are the same, recommend using 32 bit float, 44.1khz, mp3 for both if you are uncertain. You can use Audacity (free open source software) to check and change formats.

# TEMPORAL UPSCALING GROUP

This  will help with motion but motion is still less than great in LTX 2.5. This will double your fps before going through the sampler, then half it again before saving out. So 24fps video in, will be 24fps out but will pass through the sampler at 48fps.

widgets_values:
# FOR SINGLE SAMPLER UPSCALE REFINER

with LTX 2.3 model try:

sigmas 0.64 to 0.66 ("constant" for straight drop off)
steps 4
no upscale on inbound is best 
euler_ancestral about best but can try lcm, dpmpp_2m or euler_ancestral_cfg_pp

with LTX 2.5 model can try:

0.75, 0.5, 0.25, 0.0
0.5, 0.35, 0.2, 0.0 
or even 0.35, 0.2, 0.0.

BEST RESULTS:

5 steps, start at 0.5 (constant).

widgets_values:
# 3 OPTIONS FOR AUDIO

I got ooms when I tested audio with lipsync but the minimal low denoise does less damage to mouth movements it still impacts it to look weak. So this is a wip where testing audio for controlling lipsync might be of benefit but also might run into problems since targetting each person talking will likely need good prompting and LTX used to be notorious for causing cloned mouth movements in people not talking.

----

choose your connector and plug it into the "audio_latent" slot of the 1st upscaler groups "LTXVConcatAVLatent" node. You dont need to bypass the others, just switch out the connector, but it might be best to bypass in some situations. also check which audio is being saved to the final Video Combine node.

1. "Empty Latent Audio" (A) (use this as default so it doesnt error)
use this if you are prompting dialogue or dont care about audio.

2. Use "Audio From Video Group" (B)
Use this if you want to keep the audio from the video all the way through and drive lipsync from it too.

3. Use "Audio-In Group" (C) if you want to drive the lipsync and dialogue from an audio file.

# [MARKDKBERRY.COM](https://markdkberry.com)

for updated info and more stuff follow

[YT channel](https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry)

[Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies)

---


## UPSCALER WORKFLOW

This is adapted from old LTX 2.3 workflows and reduced to provide only an upscaler to 3mp (you can set the size to whatever you want).

It works by loading up a video you want detailed, and you set the upscale size (recommended 2304 x ? - I use widescreen but I suggest limiting the long side to 2304 as a first run, 8 second video takes 17 mins on my 3060 RTX as a guide I oom above it). That is all you need to set (other than you choice of models). It will then auto-pull the first frame and use that as guide. It then passes through a single sampler at low denoise and minimal sigma steps. The temporal upscale takes it from 24fps to 48fps and then back down again before saving the video out.

I have put 2.3 vae video model in because its currently quicker than the 2.5 vae video model. Otherwise set everything to use LTX 2.5 and whatever memory management you have setup on your rig.

More info and updates to this workflow can be found here [https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows/tree/main/workflows_by_model/LTX25](https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows/tree/main/workflows_by_model/LTX25) check the readme for the latest info
